Family Welfare & Contraception

Family welfare and contraception in India — goals, methods, counselling and the right of couples to choose.

In simple words

Family welfare programmes help couples plan the number and spacing of children, according to their own choice. Contraception is the method used.

Family welfare objectives

  • Reduce maternal and child mortality
  • Space pregnancies for the mother’s recovery
  • Allow families to choose a small family size
  • Reduce unsafe abortion
  • Prevent teenage pregnancy

Methods of contraception

Method Key points
Combined oral contraceptive pill Regular daily; failure if missed; not for smokers over 35 or with history of clotting
Condom Protects against infection as well
Copper-T IUCD Long acting, 5-10 years; check threads; avoid if pelvic infection
PPIUCD Inserted within 48 hours of delivery
Hormonal injection (DMPA) Every 12 weeks
Emergency contraception Within 72 hours
Natural methods Calendar method, withdrawal, exclusive breastfeeding
Sterilisation Female tubectomy and male vasectomy; permanence
Injectable contraceptive-antigonadotropin (Centchroman) Weekly pill, non-hormonal option

🔴 Couple choice is protected

The couple’s choice of contraceptive is respected and private. Never pressure, label or mislead. Give information about all methods, including side effects and follow-up.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Family welfare aims at spacing, choice and maternal and child health.
  2. Copper IUCD is a long-acting reversible method for 5-10 years.
  3. Sterilisation is a permanent method — female tubectomy or male vasectomy.
  4. Emergency contraception must be used within 72 hours.
  5. Contraception is the couple’s choice and never coerced.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Oral contraceptive may cause spotting, headache and nausea.
  2. Condoms also protect against sexually transmitted infections.
  3. IUCD should be avoided in active pelvic infection.
  4. Breastfeeding helps space pregnancies only if exclusive.
  5. Sterilisation counselling requires informed consent.

📌 Memory trick

PPIUCD goes in Post-Placental (within 48 hours), Intra-Uterine, Contraceptive Device.

60-second revision

  • Family welfare, small healthy family, planned spacing.
  • Methods: natural, barrier, hormonal, IUCD, permanent.
  • Emergency pills within 72 hours.
  • IUCD for the long term; check the thread monthly.
  • Sterilisation as a permanent choice with informed consent.
  • Counselling must be respectful.

Test yourself

A long-acting reversible method is:

Answer: B. The copper intrauterine device is long-acting and reversible, lasting 5 to 10 years.

Emergency contraception is used within:

Answer: B. Emergency contraception is most effective when taken within 72 hours of unprotected sex.

Which method protects against sexually transmitted infection too?

Answer: A. Condoms provide the dual benefit of contraception and protection from infection.

A PPIUCD is inserted:

Answer: B. Post-Placental IUCD is inserted within 48 hours after childbirth.

Counselling for family planning requires:

Answer: B. The couple must be informed about options, effects and follow-up, and decide freely.
